title: Book Two · Chapter 8: A Shelf for Books
story:
There are two boxes beside Miss Wu's desk on Monday.

Ronan sees them when he comes in. The first lid is open. The second box is still closed. A small book lies on top of a thick one.

“Are those for us?” Leo asks.

“For the class,” Miss Wu says. “We can borrow them.”

She holds up the small book. A corner of its cover is loose.

“We will check them first. Not all this morning. We still have lessons.”

Ronan carries his bag to the desk. He wants the first turn with the books. So does Leo.

At break, Miss Wu calls four children over. Mei and Jun join the boys.

Miss Wu shows them the low shelf at the back. It holds paper and an old basket of wooden shapes.

“We can use the right side for books,” she says.

“Where will the basket go?” Mei asks.

Miss Wu points to a lower space. “Down there. Leave room to take it out.”

Jun moves the basket carefully. Two shapes fall behind it. He reaches for them, but Miss Wu asks him to wait. She pulls the basket forward herself. Then he can get both shapes.

Ronan takes the paper from the shelf. Some sheets are clean. Others have writing on one side.

“Can we use these for names?” he asks.

“Keep the clean ones aside. We will need them.”

Leo wipes the shelf with a cloth. He makes a long wet line.

“Not too much water,” Mei says. “The books will sit here.”

He squeezes the cloth into the bowl and tries again.

The shelf is dry by the end of lunch. Ronan brings one box with Jun. They put it on the floor first. The box is heavy, but each book is easy to lift.

Mei lays the books on two desks. Leo makes a tall pile.

“It will fall,” she says.

“It is standing.”

Then Jun takes a thin book from the middle. The top leans to one side. Leo catches it with both hands.

“Now it is sitting,” Ronan says.

They make two lower piles instead.

Miss Wu looks at the books. She gives each child a small job. Mei checks covers. Jun looks for torn pages. Leo puts the books in a row. Ronan counts them.

At first he counts one book twice. The covers are almost the same. He separates them and starts again.

“Eighteen,” he says.

“Leave the second box closed for now,” Miss Wu tells them. “We can finish tomorrow.”

Ronan looks at its lid. He wants to open it, but he brings the counting paper to her instead.

He passes the row of books on his way to his desk. One book is about a garden. Another has a train on the front.

Leo stops beside the train.

“I want this one.”

“So do I.”

“Then we need two trains.”

Ronan looks at the small row of books. “Or two turns.”

Miss Wu calls the class to sit down. They leave the train beside the garden, on the dry shelf.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

borrow＝借用；squeeze＝挤压；separate＝分开；a row＝一排。

## 理解问题

1. 四个孩子分别做了哪些事？
2. 为什么他们改成两堆较矮的书？

## 读句子

They / make two lower piles / instead.＝他们／改成堆出两堆较矮的书。
